profile.summary: GenerRNA is a generative language model that writes new RNA sequences. It is a decoder-only transformer, the same style as GPT, trained on millions of natural RNA sequences so that it can sample sequences it has never seen. It takes no structure, label or alignment as input: either sample from it as it is, or fine-tune it on a family or a function first.

summary_quotes.text: GenerRNA is a generative RNA language model based on a Transformer decoder-only architecture.
can generate novel, realistic RNA sequences **without any structural input, functional label, or sequence alignment**

GenerRNA enable you to generate RNA sequences in a zero-shot manner for exploring the RNA space, or to fine-tune the model using a specific dataset for generating RNAs belonging to a particular family or possessing specific characteristics.
GenerRNA is pre-trained on large-scale RNA sequences and capable of generating novel RNA sequences

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GenerRNA is a decoder-only transformer of 350 million parameters: 24 layers with a model dimension of 1280, the same shape as GPT-2-medium. It is trained to predict the next token, with no labels. Sequences are split by a byte-pair encoding tokenizer with a vocabulary of 1024, so one token covers several nucleotides. The context window is 1024 tokens, about 4000 nucleotides. In preprocessing, U was replaced with T and ambiguity codes were kept. Generation is sampling: sampling.py writes new sequences from a checkpoint and a tokenizer.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two checkpoints exist. The Hugging Face repository pfnet/GenerRNA holds model_updated.pt, which the card recommends and calls the longer-context model trained on deduplicated data, and keeps the original model under experiment_data/historical_version/ as four split parts with its own tokenizer. The GitHub repository pfnet-research/GenerRNA opens by saying it is not the newest version and points to Hugging Face. Each checkpoint has its own tokenizer directory, and they must be paired correctly. A result should name the checkpoint file, its tokenizer and the Hugging Face revision; this page read revision 43efbbd0.

notes: Three sources disagree on the pretraining corpus size: the GitHub README says 30M sequences and 17B nucleotides, the Hugging Face card says 16.09M and about 17.4B, and the paper says about 16 million and 11.6 billion. All three are reported in the Training data fact and flagged in gaps; a human should decide which to show. The GitHub repository states plainly that it is not the newest version and points to Hugging Face, so the card was treated as the current source. The model card also names a third code location, github.com/ekkkkki/GenerRNA, which was not fetched. git-lfs is likely needed to pull the checkpoint, and the pinned transformers version (4.33.0.dev0) is a development release that may not install from PyPI; neither point is stated in the sources.
